rv.q: For all its throwaway charm, “[title of show]” can lay claim to a certain worthy pedigree.
But the show is so desperate to be loved - and yet so defiantly defensive and so oddly pleased with its success that there's no room for audiences to discover the endearing smartness for themselves.
What was once a rigorously original meditation on artistic inspiration is now (to quote from the show) a "toothless, gutless, and crotchless" backstage drama with an unusually peppy setup.

cn.t: This meta-musical about writing a musical charms with its clever, self-referential concept, but critics are divided on whether its scrappy off-Broadway appeal translates to the big stage.

vs.sum: The Lyceum Theatre offers good sightlines and a charming Beaux Arts ambiance, but suffers from cramped seating and small restrooms. Ideal for intimate dramas, but patrons should be prepared for less comfort during their visit.

acc.note: 4 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No elevator. Infrared devices available.
